checked_sources: Sadekar et al., arXiv:2311.11128, accessible version Eq. 5 and associated sampling paragraph
correctness.rationale: An independent backward check tracks the initial ancestors of one strategy and one game label sampled at time t from independently uniform individuals. Write a=p_s/2, b=p_g/2. When the two current ancestral carriers coincide, going one step backward separates them if that carrier was focal, its model was distinct and exactly one trait copied; the probability is s=(N−1)(a+b−2ab)/N². For distinct carriers, the probability of joining is j=(a+b)/N²: either carrier was focal, had the other as model and copied the tracked trait. The two-state chain starts with coincident probability 1/N; after t steps that probability is π+(1/N−π)(1−s−j)^t with π=j/(s+j). Exchangeability gives a uniform individual conditional on coincidence and a uniform ordered distinct pair otherwise. Their initial joint label probabilities are h_sg and (N r_s q_g−h_sg)/(N−1). Substituting these gives the stated transient formula with λ=s+j and θ=(Nπ−1)/(N−1)=2ab/[N(a+b−2ab)+2ab], exactly the coefficient in the original propensities. A prescribed block where all other individuals in turn copy both traits from individual 1 has uniformly positive probability, yielding almost-sure joint consensus. Bounded convergence turns the transient limit into the fixation law for each arbitrary pair of labels. Excluding self multiplies both nonzero ancestry transition probabilities by N/(N−1), giving the same terminal law and the faster discrete-time rate. Finally, θ is strictly increasing in a and b; differentiating in a gives 2Nb²/[N(a+b−2ab)+2ab]². The maximum at a=b=1/2 is exactly 1/(N+1).
residual_risks: Source checker was read, not run. The finite binary checks corroborate the terminal law, not the arbitrary-label or finite-time claims by themselves. The accessible preprint validates the well-mixed mechanism; the journal equation number was not checked directly.

evidence: Kamm et al. propagate a Moran distribution from a stationary starting law in Eq. (2); their Theorem 1 computes the coalescent's two-locus sampling probability under variable sizes using stationary initialization and continuous-time matrix exponentials. The two-layer voter paper treats another copying rule. Sadekar et al. cover positive selection and structured networks as well as the well-mixed case, but the inspected mechanism does not supply the fixation formula.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The prior theorem's stationary initial law does not cover the arbitrary deterministic initial haplotype table and its dependence on h_sg. Turning mutation off in its stationary-start scheme does not produce those arbitrary initial configurations. Nor can the continuous-time exponential be specialized to the geometric factor for the shared-pair discrete chain without a new kernel identification and reduction.

evidence: The exact earlier Fermi rule specializes to a=p_s/2 and b=p_g/2. Standard two-locus ancestry supplies the idea of coalescing and splitting carriers. The exact two-state transition probabilities for this shared-pair update must still be identified, then combined with a deterministic initial label table and the absorption argument. None of the inspected earlier statements gives this exact fixed-initial-data solution or its discrete-step dependence.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the previously specified model and the established ancestry framework. The distinct contribution is the quantitative evaluation, not the abstract two-state chain solution or the discovery that linked traits can correlate. A matrix propagation formula for a stationary-start comparison model is not a scalar evaluated fixation law for this different initialization and update rule.

evidence: Sadekar et al. use the same ordered pair and independent game/strategy decisions: the accessible preprint rule gives Π=1/2 at zero strength. Vega-Oliveros et al. instead use separate neighbors and tolerance-dependent copying. Kamm et al.'s finite Moran process uses whole-haplotype overwrites and reciprocal crossovers; the earlier voter catalog hit uses coalescing walkers to compute same-attribute stationary covariances on an infinite tree.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Both continuous-time clone/crossover ancestry and the discrete co-imitation ancestry can be reduced to two coincidence states for one sampled lineage per trait. The transition mechanisms differ: clone events can merge distinct carriers and swaps can separate a common carrier, whereas here single-trait copies do both and only one forward individual is updated. The two-state generator can be rate matched to the co-imitation transition matrix minus the identity, but that does not identify the full forward chains or the discrete-time law with the continuous-time one. The exact well-mixed neutral update is indeed an earlier model specialization, not a new model.

evidence: The inspected catalog entries compute stationary pair correlations for infinite-tree broadcast voters and for competing zealots on a bipartite network, respectively. Kamm et al. generate tables of two-locus sampling likelihoods under their demographic model, not fixed-label terminal probabilities for independent co-imitation.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: These are different exact functions of different systems. A matching law must retain the distinction between independent versus shared sampling of the two initial labels and express the weights for the given finite N and copy propensities; none of the inspected tables has those semantics.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct result is the explicit terminal joint table for arbitrary fixed initial paired labels and the discrete-step rate for the same neutral co-imitation mechanism. Ancestor separation/coincidence is standard, and the inspected two-locus Moran process even gives an analogous two-state calculation after rate matching. Its stated sampling theorems have different initialization and dynamics, however, and do not give the fixed-initial-data co-imitation law by substitution into their hypotheses. The model source supplies the exact update mechanism but not the neutral law.
residual_risks: An unexamined two-locus fixation or shared-update voter result could contain an equivalent finite-time or terminal identity. Journal-version equation numbering in Sadekar et al. could not be checked; the accessible preprint establishes the mechanism directly.

checked_sources: Sadekar et al., arXiv:2311.11128, well-mixed imitation mechanism
value.rationale: The exact joint table separates association caused solely by shared neutral copying from association that would require selection. The coefficient quantifies the effect at any N and propensity pair, with a sharp maximum, while the transient identity measures how long that dependence takes to build up under either pair-sampling convention. This supplies a useful comparison for the already studied coevolving game/strategy model, not merely a proof that consensus occurs.
residual_risks: The benchmark does not apply unchanged to nonzero selection, structured graphs, mutation, or separately sampled models for the two attributes.
